title: Protocol adapter + migration playbook for OpenTelemetry upgrade and low-lock demultiplexer
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Upgrade our runtime observability stack to a newer OpenTelemetry runtime (target v1.16 SDK and OTLP/Protobuf v0.16) while adding a small compatibility adapter that lets old exporters coexist with the new OTLP envelopes. Primary focus is to remove a global mutex hotspot in span emission, reduce allocation churn in trace/log envelopes, and produce a tested migration path with canary/rollback steps. Scope: (1) Implement a lightweight protocol adapter that accepts both old JSON-enveloped logs/traces and new OTLP envelopes and does zero-copy demux into the exporter pipeline. (2) Introduce a lock-free demultiplexer (per-tenant ring buffer + single-writer per shard) to reduce contention from 30% cpu spent in span emit critical path to <8%. (3) Replace current tracing hooks with a small context-free span factory that emits pre-sized buffers and reuses KV cache objects to reduce GC pauses. (4) Add a migration playbook: compatibility layer, automated canary on 3% traffic, metrics and alerts to stop and rollback on error budget regressions, and an in-place fallback to legacy exporter. Acceptance criteria: - Upgrade validation: OTEL SDK v1.16 passes our unit and integration tests, no semantic regressions in span attributes. - Perf targets: end-to-end p95 span emit latency reduced by at least 10% in the hot path; total CPU consumption for span handling reduced by >=15% on representative load. - Memory/GC: per-host heap increase <8% while allocation churn drops by >=30%. - Stability: Canary on internal dev cluster for 72h with no SLO regressions before broad rollout. - Rollback plan and automation documented (playbook stored in Confluence). Out-of-scope: changes to external observability providers (we only adapt/translate), replacing the metrics storage backend, and any customer-facing schema changes. Risks and mitigations: - OTLP envelope incompatibilities: mitigated with versioned adapter and exhaustive schema tests. - Regressions under p99 tail: mitigation via small canary and synthetic load tests. - Security/PII: adapter will preserve redaction rules; we will run a quick security review before rollout.
